title: lore check and sync spawn one quest task view per task; use one task list per run cached by the .quest tree hash
description: DEC-282 item 1, filed from ODOC-610 (opum-doc, 2026-11-18T23:03Z). VERBATIM: 'lore-cli, with quest-cli for any field gap: one quest task list --json per run, never a per-task view. Missing fields are added to list's JSON (or a multi-id view) by quest-cli. Cache per run keyed by the .quest tree hash. Proof: measured at about 2000 tasks before and after, plus a test that the quest spawn count is bounded regardless of task count.' CONTEXT from the report: lore check and sync spawn one quest task view <id> --json per task, about 9 at a time, confirmed at src/adapters/quest.ts:456; 83 s wall per check at 574 tasks; on 2026-11-12 four to five concurrent runs made about 45 quest processes, a load of about 128, and a fleet shutdown. FIELD GAP MEASURED HERE on quest 0.14.1, 786 tasks: the lore:tasks rollup needs only id, title, status and the task file, and task list --json already carries id, title, status and path (path covers the file), so the per-task views are pure waste on this path. Fields detail() reads that list does NOT carry: subtasks, reporter and revision (all three exit 2 as unknown fields); file is covered by path. references, modifiedFiles and finalSummary ARE populated by list, checked against records that actually hold values rather than a null from a record that has none. Ships in the next lore/quest pair (DEC-282 items 1-4 ship together).

acceptanceCriteria.text: One quest task list --json per check and per sync run on the rollup path; no per-task task view spawns (measured: zero on that path).
The list read is cached per run, keyed by the .quest tree hash, and a changed tree invalidates the cache.
Measured at about 2000 tasks before and after, recording spawn count and wall time.
A test asserts the quest spawn count is bounded regardless of task count (N tasks, constant spawns).
Any field gap is named with the quest-cli ticket that adds it; today the rollup needs no gap, and subtasks, reporter and revision are named as the fields list lacks if a consumer needs them.

implementationNotes:
Built 2026-11-19 on branch fix/LCLI-791-one-quest-list-per-run. Rollup path (check, sync) now reads ONE quest task list per run via a new optional TrackerAdapter.taskRollup, cached across runs at .lore/cache/quest/task-list.json under sha256(quest version + every file under .quest). Zero task views on that path; lore tasks, link and orphans still view per task (unchanged); a backend without taskRollup falls back to per-task views.
Evidence: test/lcli791-quest-rollup.test.ts (6 tests): control = per-task path costs N views; total spawns identical for 3, 30 and 300 tasks with 0 views and 1 list; gatherReconciliation rows identical; missing id gives the same not_found; second run over an unchanged tree makes 0 list calls, a changed tree re-reads; corrupt cache is a miss. Test commit predicted the pre-build state (import failure); mutant forcing the per-task fallback gives 5 red with the control green. Full bun test: 5423 pass, 3 fail, all LCLI-614 real-quest race tests (known local pair-lock artifact, CI is the judge). typecheck and biome clean.
MEASURED, real quest 0.14.1 on this repo at 794 tasks (NOT the 2000 AC3 names, and the replaced operations rather than lore end to end, because the local pair lock refuses a real lore run): 794 quest task view at 8 concurrent = 26.5 s wall and 794 spawns; one quest task list = 0.146 s and 1 spawn. AC3 therefore stays UNCHECKED pending a 2000-task measurement.
FIELD GAP: none for the rollup (id, title, status, path all in list). task list lacks subtasks, reporter and revision, which only viewTask/detail consumers (lore link, lore tasks) read; no quest-cli ticket needed today.

ROUND-2 DESIGN, as merged in #735 (e8764dfb) and refined in the follow-up PR; this SUPERSEDES the first note above where they differ. The rollup read is `quest task list --include-archived --json` (the pinned 0.14.1 accepts the flag; task view resolves archived records, so the list must). It is served through TaskRollupIndex.lookup(id): ids and aliases both resolve, a reference matching more than one record raises a conflict naming task_reference_ambiguous (as quest's findTask does) instead of picking a winner, and only the LOOKED-UP records are validated, aliases included, so an unlinked malformed record cannot fail a rollup. The cross-run cache at .lore/cache/quest/task-list.json is keyed by sha256 of the lore version, the quest version and every file under .quest (questListCacheKey), and a write re-hashes the tree and is skipped unless the key still holds, so a quest write landing during the list is never cached under the pre-write key (remaining window: an exact A-to-B-to-A revert inside one ~0.15 s list call). lore tasks, link and orphans still view per task. Tests: test/lcli791-quest-rollup.test.ts, 23 tests, each new behaviour with a mutant that goes red. AC3 stays UNCHECKED: it needs the 2000-task end-to-end measurement against a pair-matched quest 0.15.0 including a WARM run (nothing yet proves a real-binary cache hit); the earlier 794-task figure times only the replaced operations.

VERDICT: APPROVE

Review of opum-ai/lore-cli#737 (LCLI-791), the round-2 follow-up to opum-ai/lore-cli#735. I worked read-only: no shell, no writes. Everything I cite from quest-cli comes from its working tree, read with Read/Grep, not from a ref or the pinned binary.

FINDINGS (all NON-BLOCKING)

1. F4 wiring is not pinned (src/adapters/quest.ts:1056, test/lcli791-quest-rollup.test.ts:266), NON-BLOCKING.
   - The new test pins only the pure helper questListCacheKey.
   - Two mutants at the call site would stay green across all 23 tests, because the key changes but stays consistent run to run:
     - treeKey returning the bare tree digest.
     - treeKey passing constant versions.
   - Against the pre-PR code the test goes red only as an import failure.
   - Low risk: the pair lock forces quest's version to equal lore's VERSION.

2. The self-alias dedupe is untested (src/adapters/quest.ts:989, `!held.includes(item)`), NON-BLOCKING.
   - The guard makes a record whose alias equals its own id count as one match, which matches findTask: it filters records, so a record matches once.
   - Dropping the guard stays green.
   - Only a hand edit can reach this case.

3. The F3 assertion passes against the pre-PR code (test:277-287), NON-BLOCKING and expected.
   - The pre-PR code already stored the list's own error (validation or drift), not not_found.
   - The assertion still does its job: it goes red under the "swallow the list error into an empty index" mutant.

4. Orphaned docblock (src/adapters/quest.ts:1016-1029), NON-BLOCKING, cosmetic.
   - questListCache's long docblock now sits directly above questListCacheKey's own docblock (:1030).
   - So questListCache (:1041) has no doc of its own, and the corrected F6 text documents nothing in tooling.

5. Case folding differs from quest (src/adapters/quest.ts:986/997), NON-BLOCKING, pre-existing from #735.
   - The index uses .toLowerCase().
   - quest's aliasKey (quest-cli src/domain/records.ts:90-93) uses caseFold(normalize("NFC")).
   - For non-ASCII references the list path can disagree with task view, in both match and ambiguity. ASCII ids behave identically.

6. The record note overclaims (.quest/tasks/LCLI-791.json, note 2), NON-BLOCKING.
   - It says "each new behaviour with a mutant that goes red". Findings 1 and 2 are counterexamples.
   - Its "23 tests" count does match the file: 10 plain, 2 collision, 1 key, 3 failing-list, 7 cache.

7. A corner case returns not_found instead of drift (src/adapters/quest.ts:993), NON-BLOCKING.
   - A record whose aliases field is not an array, for example the string "OLD", is not indexed by alias. Looking up "OLD" therefore returns not_found.
   - The per-task path would get quest's parse failure instead.
   - This is still a loud ok:false and never a per-task spawn, so it does not touch DEC-282 item 1.

CHECK ANSWERS

- Ambiguity (Q2): matches findTask (quest-cli src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts:1397-1408).
  - Every id and alias goes into one byReference map, and more than one match throws task_reference_ambiguous.
  - Both shapes are covered: an id that is another record's alias (collide:"id") and an alias shared by two records (collide:"alias").
  - Error type: the per-task path gets "conflict" because RecordConflictError.kind is "conflict" (quest-cli records.ts:6-7), and lore's validErrorType accepts it. I read the class; I did not trace the stderr rendering.
  - Tested both ways:
    - Refused: test:249-262. Both cases are red against the pre-PR code, which resolved them to the first match or the canonical id.
    - Resolved when unambiguous: test:171 (OLD-2.1 to T-2) and test:208 (archived A-1 and OLD-A), both now running through the new index, plus the T-3 control inside the collision test.

- Fail-closed (Q3): yes.
  - resolveRollupDetails (reconcile-shared.ts:263-287) falls back to per-task views only when adapter.taskRollup is undefined.
  - A list failure is stored against every id, and a lookup throw is stored against its own id. Neither causes a spawn.
  - A linked record with malformed aliases now raises drift (quest.ts:1010), and the cached path validates the same way (rollupItem keeps aliases).

- Can each new test fail (Q4): yes.
  - Red against the pre-PR code: F1 badAliases (test:238) and both collision tests.
  - Red only as an import failure against the pre-PR code: the F4 key test.
  - Passes against the pre-PR code but goes red under its target mutant: the F3 not_found assertion.

- Regression (Q5): none.
  - taskRollup is unchanged: one list, zero views.
  - Validation is still lazy, and the re-hash before a cache write is intact.
  - The key composition changed (sha of version prefix plus tree digest), which costs only a one-time cache miss.
  - The CHANGELOG line still says a corrupt cache is "only a miss". That stays true if corrupt means unparseable; the code comment now carves out the tampered-but-key-matching case.

AC3 MEASURED 2026-11-21 (specialist verifier unit, read-only on the repo; scratch fixture, real pair-matched quest). lore HEAD c28290c2d2966c756de9a44cb94832cf116be64b (contains #735 e8764dfb and #737 7329ae1f), BASE 5de72d1b6addee06f48308e30be8ec607641204c (parent of #735). Both lore 0.15.0. quest: quest-cli dev 1cce24f1e8cce9b2d9ef70e399a1dda5af12c2a8 local build, darwin-arm64, unsigned, run in place, `--version` prints 0.15.0 (the shim execs it and passes --version through, so the pair lock accepted it). bun 1.4.4 (/opt/homebrew/bin/bun, the pinned one). Fixture: real quest workspace of 2000 records (1800 tasks/, 100 completed/, 100 archive/tasks/), `quest doctor` healthy; docs variant fix5 = 100 distinct linked ids (5%), variant fixall = 2000 distinct linked ids (worst case). Spawns counted by a PATH shim logging argv; `task list --include-archived --json` returned exactly 2000 rows (control on this repo's real .quest: 799 records, 799 rows).
RESULT. HEAD spawn count is constant in the number of linked tasks: check 7 cold / 6 warm, sync 10 cold / 9 warm, identical at 100 and at 2000 linked tasks. BASE grows one spawn per linked task: check 106 -> 2006, sync 109 -> 2009. Warm HEAD made ZERO task list spawns (a real cache hit; .lore/cache/quest/task-list.json holds 2000 items); cold HEAD made exactly one. Wall time (load-sensitive, load average high): HEAD about 1 to 2 s at both sizes; BASE about 7 to 9 s at 100 linked and 107 to 144 s at 2000. Every run exited 0 and stdout was byte-identical base vs head in all 8 cold/warm pairs.
CONCURRENCY, 5 concurrent cold `lore check`: HEAD peak 5 quest processes and 35 total spawns (5 task list, 0 task view) at both 100 and 2000 linked; BASE peak 41 / 40 and 530 / 10030 total spawns, reproducing the 2026-11-12 shape (about 45 processes). The 5 HEAD runs each issued one task list because they started before any cache was written; a warm wave was not separately run.
NOT MEASURED, do not read beyond: macOS arm64 local build only (not CI, Linux or Windows); the 50 ms process sampler can miss a sub-50 ms spike, the shim-log totals are exact; the BASE tree came from git archive plus bun install, not a second in-repo worktree; the replaced operations were not re-measured beyond base-vs-head; a local full bun test was not part of this. AC3 is therefore met for the single-run claim; the lock work (LCLI-792, #746) is what bounds concurrent runs further.
